# Ellen West

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)</sub>

## Appearance

Ellen is dark, stately, and massive in figure. She has thick black hair, black eyebrows, and eyes of a clear, slaty blue. She possesses a deep, mellow, pleasant voice with a hint of masculinity.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P54](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0054), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c22 P8](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0008)_

## Personality

Despite a stern and forbidding initial look, Ellen is very jolly, possessing a hearty laugh and a good sense of humour. She has an exceptionally keen understanding of politics and world affairs, often matching or exceeding the men in her community. She is known to be remarkably strong-willed, resolute, and unyielding, sometimes to the point of stubbornness.

_Sources: [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c21 P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008), [v5 c21 P13](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0013), [v5 c22 P8](../source/v05-c22.md#nw-v05-c22-p0008), [v5 c32 P47](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0047)_

## Goals

- uphold her life and promises made with her sister  <sub>[v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c21 P25](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0025)</sub>

## History

Ellen West grew up in the West homestead on the hill, living with her mother and sister Rosemary after her father and brother passed away. In her girlhood, she had a romantic relationship with Norman Douglas, which ended after a silly quarrel and led to Norman marrying someone else out of spite. Following her mother's death, Ellen and Rosemary lived quietly together for many years, bound by a mutual pledge not to marry and leave the other alone. When the minister John Meredith moved to the Glen, Ellen formed a strong friendship with him based on their shared interest in politics and world events. Later, Norman Douglas rekindled his love for Ellen after seeing her at church, and after much coaxing and persistent courtship, he arranged to marry her.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P66](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0066), [v5 c13 P25](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0025), [v5 c15 P31](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0031), [v5 c21 P8](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0008), [v5 c21 P15](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0015), [v5 c21 P25](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0025), [v5 c26 P17](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0017), [v5 c34 P6](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0006), [v5 c35 P7](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0007)_

## Quotes

> St. George, this world would be a dull place without the men, I’ll admit, but I’m almost tempted to wish there wasn’t one of ‘em in it. Look at the trouble and bother they’ve made right here, George—torn our happy old life completely up by the roots, Saint. John Meredith began it and Norman Douglas has finished it. And now both of them have to go into limbo. Norman is the only man I ever met who agrees with me that the Kaiser of Germany is the most dangerous creature alive on this earth—and I can’t marry this sensible person because my sister is stubborn and I’m stubborner. Mark my words, St. George, the minister would come back if she raised her little finger. But she won’t George—she’ll never do it—she won’t even crook it—and I don’t dare meddle, Saint. I won’t sulk, George; Rosemary didn’t sulk, so I’m determined I won’t either, Saint; Norman will tear up the turf, but the long and short of it is, St. George, that all of us old fools must just stop thinking of marrying. Well, well, ‘despair is a free man, hope is a slave,’ Saint. So now come into the house, George, and I’ll solace you with a saucerful of cream. Then there will be one happy and contented creature on this hill at least.  <sub>[v5 c32 P47](../source/v05-c32.md#nw-v05-c32-p0047)</sub>
